Combine indicators into a composite index

Source: R/idx.R
idx_combine.Rd

Takes a weighted arithmetic or geometric mean of indicator columns, usually after idx_normalize().

Usage

idx_combine(
  data,
  cols,
  weights = NULL,
  method = c("arithmetic", "geometric"),
  name = "index"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or sf object with one row per unit.

cols

<tidy-select> Numeric indicator columns to combine.

weights

Optional non-negative weights, one per selected column, either in the order selected or named by column. They are rescaled to sum to 1. NULL (the default) weights every column equally.

method

"arithmetic" for the weighted mean \(\sum_j w_j x_j\), or "geometric" for the weighted geometric mean \(\prod_j x_j^{w_j}\). Under the geometric mean a high value on one indicator makes up less for a low value on another.

name

Name of the new index column.

Value

data with a new column named name.

Details

The geometric mean is defined only for positive values. idx_combine() does not shift or truncate values to make them positive, because the size of any shift changes the result. It stops with an error that counts the values at or below zero. Min-max and rank normalization both set the lowest unit to 0, so rescale to a positive range, such as 1 to 100, before asking for a geometric mean.

A unit missing any indicator gets a missing index.

See also

idx_normalize(), idx_sensitivity().

Examples

cities <- data.frame(
  city = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
  share = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9),
  isolation = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.8, 0.7)
)
cities |>
  idx_normalize(c(share, isolation), method = "z") |>
  idx_combine(c(share, isolation), weights = c(share = 2, isolation = 1))
#>   city      share isolation      index
#> 1    a -1.2124356 -1.050210 -1.1583604
#> 2    b -0.1732051 -0.630126 -0.3255121
#> 3    c  0.1732051  1.050210  0.4655401
#> 4    d  1.2124356  0.630126  1.0183324

idx_combine(cities, c(share, isolation), method = "geometric")
#>   city share isolation     index
#> 1    a   0.2       0.3 0.2449490
#> 2    b   0.5       0.4 0.4472136
#> 3    c   0.6       0.8 0.6928203
#> 4    d   0.9       0.7 0.7937254
